whatThisIs: Zoning constraint and reference data published by the City of Edmonton under an open licence. It carries no price, no offer, no ownership and no market status of any kind, and it is not inventory. It answers what rules govern a parcel, not what a person may buy.
whatThisCannotAnswer: Which district a specific parcel falls in. Polygon geometry is not baked (about 8 MB of GeoJSON, measured 2026-08-14), so Aura links to the City's own zoning map for the parcel-specific answer.

Minimum Site area, Setbacks, minimum Site width and minimum dwelling size. Those are in Zoning Bylaw 20001 text rather than in an open dataset, so each district carries the City's URL for its own section and Aura records the numbers as unknown.
Servicing, potable water, private sewage and legal access. Those are parcel and utility facts; no district record can stand in for them.

modifierConvention.note: Zoning Bylaw 20001 states the convention in its own text. The MU Zone's Table 4.1 gives the maximum Height as “The number (in metres) following the Modifier ‘h’ as indicated on the Zoning Map”, and the maximum Floor Area Ratio as the number following the Modifier ‘f’. Zones that carry an h modifier therefore publish their own height ceiling on the map itself. Zones that do not carry one leave it in bylaw text, and Aura records it as unknown.

interpreted.h: Maximum Height, in metres, per the zone's own Site and Building Regulations table.
interpreted.f: Maximum Floor Area Ratio, per the same table.

modifierConvention.caution: A district ceiling is not a parcel permission. Overlays, special areas, Direct Control provisions and site-specific rules can lower it, and none of that is decided by the zone code alone.

refusedSources.title: Vacant Land Inventory
refusedSources.reason: A snapshot whose zone codes are mostly from the repealed Zoning Bylaw 12800. Only 11 of its 36 zone codes still exist on the current zoning map (31%), so joining it to Bylaw 20001 districts would have published decade-old zoning under today's retrieval date.

overlayBylaws.note: 17 of 35 overlays carry a bylaw number other than 20001 — these are special areas the City carried forward under their original number, and the number is reproduced as the City publishes it. Bylaw 12800 is REPEALED. Each overlay states its own bylawInForce so this cannot be read as current regulation. Aura does not interpret a repealed overlay's rules.
